metadata.notes: Core publication eligibility not implied; alternate leading questions and independent source dependency recorded. No images used.

reviews.title_after: Storm Dudley sweeps northern Britain as another storm approaches
reviews.location_after: Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England
reviews.core_fact: Storm Dudley brought damaging winds to northern parts of the UK on February 16–17, 2022, before the separate Storm Eunice arrived February 18.
reviews.source_dependence: The Met Office storm-season retrospective and independently published UK news corroborate the February 16–17 Dudley window, but reporter wind figures rely partly on the Met Office.
reviews.unverified_cautions: February 17 captures the trailing phase of Dudley, NOT Eunice's February 18 peak or Franklin on Feb20–21. ITV reported forecast and observed gusts with distinct times; do not label every 80 mph figure as observed Feb17.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original synoptic maps of Dudley vs later Eunice, with dated pressure centers and observational station gusts

reviews.title_after: Severe Tropical Cyclone Larry slams Queensland near Innisfail
reviews.location_after: Innisfail and coastal Far North Queensland, Australia
reviews.core_fact: Cyclone Larry crossed the Queensland coast near Innisfail around daybreak March 20, 2006, at Australian tropical cyclone Category 4 intensity in BoM's post-analysis.
reviews.source_dependence: Australian Bureau of Meteorology post-analysis is source of classification; NASA's near-landfall satellite scene independently confirms timing/location but not surface wind speed.
reviews.unverified_cautions: BoM history lists Australian Category 4 landfall around 0700 AEST March20 (2100 UTC March19), while older research narrations describe brief pre-landfall Category 5. Australian cyclone categories use a different 10-minute sustained-wind basis from U.S. Saffir–Simpson ratings; NEVER equate numerically.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original 19–20 March local-vs-UTC cyclone track with Innisfail landfall and Australia-specific intensity label

reviews.title_after: Irish and UK airspace begins reopening amid Icelandic volcanic ash
reviews.location_after: Ireland and United Kingdom, North Atlantic and western Europe
reviews.core_fact: On April 20, 2010 aviation regulators authorized a phased evening resumption of Irish and UK air services following extensive airspace restrictions caused by Eyjafjallajökull volcanic ash.
reviews.source_dependence: Irish Aviation Authority original operational statement is independently reported by RTÉ the same date; RTÉ relies on regulator for exact opening time but separately reports travel effects.
reviews.unverified_cautions: April20 is the regulatory decision/reopening phase, NOT the volcano's eruption start (April14 summit eruption) or every European airport's reopening. Irish Aviation Authority statement was 20:45 and authorized flights from 21:00 local, but airlines resumed only gradually over subsequent days.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original airspace risk and ash-advection timeline ending with 20 April phased reopening decision

reviews.title_after: Mount St. Helens erupts as upper-level winds spread ash eastward
reviews.location_after: Mount St. Helens, southwest Washington and downwind Inland Northwest
reviews.core_fact: The May 18, 1980 Mount St. Helens eruption produced a large ash column that was transported eastward by winds, spreading ash into the Inland Northwest and beyond.
reviews.source_dependence: USGS original eruption/ash transport study and Smithsonian research synthesis share eruption measurement history, but the Smithsonian adds independent eruptive sequence context.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The ash is volcanically generated, not a thunderstorm/anvil. The 8:32 AM PDT eruption, May18 ashfall and May19 satellite plume positions are DIFFERENT date/observation windows; plume altitudes vary by pulse and cannot be labeled a single measured height. No permission to reuse USGS/NOAA imagery automatically.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original vertical wind profile and May18–19 ash trajectory cross-section, not a reused NASA/USGS photo

reviews.title_after: Training thunderstorms produce catastrophic flash floods around Rainelle
reviews.location_after: Rainelle and Greenbrier County, West Virginia
reviews.core_fact: Thunderstorms repeatedly moved over Greenbrier County on June 23, 2016, causing destructive flash flooding around Rainelle and other West Virginia communities.
reviews.source_dependence: Original NCEI Rainelle Storm Data report and USGS later flood-inundation data include independent streamgage/high-water-mark methodology, but meteorological rainfall inputs overlap NWS observations.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The NCEI Rainelle local event segment is not all West Virginia flooding. NWS June23 rain and USGS June23–24 high-water marks/peak flows have different valid times, some impacts and aerial imagery date June24. Rain recurrence statistics refer to specified durations/locations, not the whole state.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Rainelle terrain and June23 training-storm radar rainfall versus June23–24 inundation chronology

reviews.title_after: A Chesapeake waterspout becomes the deadly Cherrystone campground tornado
reviews.core_fact: A waterspout developed over Chesapeake Bay and moved ashore at Cherrystone campground on July 24, 2014, producing a surveyed EF1 tornado.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Wakefield storm survey provides tornado classification; local government emergency declaration independently documents exact occurrence but not EF-scale engineering intensity.
reviews.unverified_cautions: NWS survey distinguishes the EF1 tornado track from a nearby broader damaging STRAIGHT-LINE wind swath and separate large hail swaths; original Cape Charles NCEI wind record was not a tornado itself. July24 tornado warning around 8:20 AM EDT, onshore impact around 8:31 AM. Photographs/Google Earth base layers in NWS newsletter are NOT granted rights for OTDwx merely by being public.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original radial wind/velocity and mini-map of distinct tornado, downburst and large-hail swaths; redraw GIS from original survey

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Bob makes a rare Category 2 landfall in Rhode Island
reviews.location_after: Block Island and Newport, Rhode Island
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Bob's eye passed Block Island and made landfall over Newport, Rhode Island, on the afternoon of August 19, 1991, as a Category 2 hurricane.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Boston regional case history and NOAA AOML historic cyclone retrospective both derive from shared post-analysis track, not independent landfall wind observations.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Regional New England impacts include Massachusetts and other states, but the Rhode Island center landfall is specifically Aug19. Category 3 applies to Bob earlier offshore, not at RI landfall; reported surge heights differ substantially between Rhode Island shoreline and Buzzards Bay.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original storm center track and category intensity at Rhode Island landfall, with separate surge-gauge observations

reviews.title_before: Tropical Storm — METRO BROWARD COUNTY, Florida
reviews.title_after: Wildfire smoke turns San Francisco's daytime sky an eerie orange
reviews.core_fact: On September 9, 2020, extreme West Coast wildfire smoke blotted out sunlight and gave the San Francisco Bay Area orange daytime skies, documented by same-day Terra MODIS satellite observations.
reviews.source_dependence: NASA satellite retrieval provides same-day smoke geography while UC Berkeley account and ground photographs independently document colored daylight; different sensing and publisher.
reviews.unverified_cautions: NASA satellite scene on Sep9 reveals atmospheric smoke plume and multiple fires; orange color in ground photos also depends on smoke optical properties and observer exposure. Thick elevated smoke and near-surface PM2.5 are NOT interchangeable without vertical-profile evidence. Do not copy third-party photos or assume NASA imagery is right-cleared for commercial/social-media use.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original September9 satellite smoke footprint with a sunlight-scattering schematic; photos only after explicit rights screening

reviews.title_before: Cold/Wind Chill — DENVER METROPOLITAN AREA, Colorado
reviews.title_after: Typhoon Cobra overwhelms the U.S. Third Fleet east of the Philippines
reviews.location_after: Philippine Sea east of the Philippines
reviews.core_fact: On December 18, 1944, elements of Admiral Halsey's Third Fleet encountered powerful Typhoon Cobra east of the Philippines, and three U.S. destroyers sank.
reviews.source_dependence: U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command primary historical analysis and National WWII Museum independent retrospective describe same operational event, with losses derived from common naval records.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The typhoon affected the force during December 14–19 while its worst losses occurred Dec18. Navy historical records report 790 deaths overall versus 775 men lost on the three destroyed destroyers; do not equate or double count. Pressure and wind estimates were made with sparse wartime instrumentation; plotted best-track positions require uncertainty notation.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original fleet positions versus estimated typhoon track, annotated with forecast uncertainty and 18 Dec date

reviews.title_after: An EF3 tornado tears across McNairy County in the March 2023 outbreak
reviews.location_after: Rose Creek and McNairy County, Tennessee
reviews.core_fact: On March 31, 2023, a long-track tornado produced EF3-level damage in McNairy County, Tennessee, during the March 31–April 1 severe outbreak.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI county record and NWS Memphis outbreak survey use the same NWS ground damage survey; a second URL is not a wholly independent wind observation.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The Rose Creek NCEI segment represents a portion of the long-track tornado. The tornado continued into April1 local time over downstream counties; do not assign entire full-track casualty/damage count to Rose Creek or March31 only.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original track by county and local-time midnight crossing, separated from neighboring tornadoes

reviews.title_after: Isaias spawns a deadly EF3 tornado in Bertie County, North Carolina
reviews.location_after: Bertie County near Windsor, North Carolina
reviews.core_fact: A tornado associated with Tropical Storm Isaias tracked through Bertie County, North Carolina early on August 4, 2020 and was rated EF3.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Wakefield event/sounding analysis and NOAA Storm Events entry both rely on one storm survey; office meteorology explains low-level SRH near a tropical boundary.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Isaias made a separate earlier cyclone landfall near Ocean Isle Beach; Bertie EF3 is a tornado within the circulation, not hurricane center landfall. EF3 peak winds are inferred from damage and NCEI county entries may split the track.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original tropical cyclone track and separate EF3 tornado path with 0–1 km helicity context

reviews.title_after: A violent F4 tornado destroys blocks of Petersburg, Virginia
reviews.location_after: Petersburg, Colonial Heights and Hopewell, Virginia
reviews.core_fact: On August 6, 1993, a violent F4 tornado struck Petersburg and nearby Virginia communities during a regional tornado outbreak.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Wakefield retrospective and NCEI historic event data share original storm surveys; local Petersburg historical account adds civilian damage chronology.
reviews.unverified_cautions: This was an F4 on the historic Fujita scale, not EF4. Local NCEI geographic segments may represent one tornado crossing cities; historic NWS survey includes 18 tornadoes in southeast Virginia that day but the count is separate from Petersburg track count.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Petersburg historic city map and F4 track with clear county/city boundaries

reviews.title_after: A violent F4 tornado strikes Madison, Mississippi during the 2001 outbreak
reviews.location_after: Madison and north Jackson suburbs, Mississippi
reviews.core_fact: An F4 tornado struck Madison, Mississippi on November 24, 2001 during a larger tornado outbreak across the state.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Jackson F4 Madison original survey and NCEI county entry share meteorological source; separate NWS survey of Bolivar/Washington highlights multiple distinct tornadoes.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The November24 episode included other separate F4 tornadoes in Bolivar and Washington counties. Avoid merging survey track or casualty figures. F4 predates EF scale and was assigned based on historical damage survey.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original multiple F4 tracks map with Madison explicitly separated from Delta tornadoes

alternate_reviews.title: F3 tornado near Camilla, Georgia
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: NCEI and NWS Tallahassee same underlying historic survey; the NWS independent synoptic write-up confirms event occurrence/date only.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: An F3-rated tornado tracked near Camilla in southwest Georgia on March 20, 2003.
alternate_reviews.caution: Historic F3 NOT EF3; Camilla had a different damaging tornado in February 2000, so do not conflate 2000 and 2003. This is an alternate for March20 Larry (different year, region and hazard).

alternate_reviews.title: Winter storm across Navajo County, Arizona
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: No independent second agency check; supplemental Storm Data publication is same underlying NOAA report.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: Original NCEI episode records a northern Arizona winter storm on March20, 2000.
alternate_reviews.caution: Original Storm Data describes several fatalities across a two-day snowfall event; neither Navajo County segment nor Mar20 independently establishes all death dates or location. Candidate remains uncorroborated.

alternate_reviews.title: A long-track EF2 tornado crosses several New Hampshire towns
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: NCEI and NWS Gray both draw on the initial damage survey. Historical NWS context confirms exact date but does not independently measure EF2 winds.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: On July 24, 2008, a lengthy EF2 tornado track crossed multiple New Hampshire towns.
alternate_reviews.caution: NCEI Leavitts Hill is one of many county portions; do not count multiple segments as separate tornadoes or infer maximum intensity along entire path. Different from July24 2014 Cherrystone, Virginia primary.

alternate_reviews.title: Multiday excessive heat in Las Vegas, Nevada
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: Only the NCEI multi-day zone source is documented. No independent date-specific station observation or fatality count verified.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: NCEI zone heat entry contains July24, 2018 within a five-day Las Vegas heat episode.
alternate_reviews.caution: The 17 heat-related deaths noted in the source refer to episode and aftermath, not July24 alone; attribution and county time windows remain unverified.
